Viscosity tolerance is 3% because published solution-viscosity data and the correlation's viscosity term carry larger uncertainty than density.

validity_note: Laliberte (2009) aqueous-electrolyte correlation for NH4Cl-water, density and viscosity. Tabulated for 2-24 wt% over 15-60 degC. Saturation is about 26 wt% NH4Cl at 15 degC, rising to about 35 wt% at 60 degC, so the 24 wt% ceiling keeps the cold end of the table below saturation. Dilute ammonium chloride is slightly less viscous than water (a known electrolyte effect) before viscosity rises again at higher strength. Heat capacity is not tabulated: the correlation's NH4Cl heat-capacity data covers only dilute solutions (to about 14 wt%), so it is omitted rather than extrapolated. Concentrations are NH4Cl by mass. Values are for preliminary design; verify against vendor data for critical service.
